title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
abstract: Deep neural nets with a large number of parameters are very powerful machine learning systems. However, overfitting is a serious problem in such networks. We propose dropout, a technique for addressing this problem by randomly dropping units during training.
key_findings: Introduced dropout: randomly dropping units during training prevents overfitting. Retention probability of 0.5 found close to optimal for hidden units across many tasks. Dropout gives major improvements over other regularization methods.
relationship_to_idea: Foundational paper — establishes the 0.5 dropout rate as a default and provides theoretical motivation for dropout as approximate model averaging.

title: Towards Dropout Training for Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Dropout training for convolutional neural networks with max-pooling dropout and channel-wise dropout strategies.
key_findings: Max-pooling dropout and fully-connected dropout produce test errors as low as 0.60% and 0.53%. Optimal dropout strategy varies by network architecture. FC dropout best for small architectures, max-pooling dropout works for both small and large.
relationship_to_idea: Directly relevant — compares different dropout strategies in CNNs and shows architecture-dependent optimal rates.

title: Survey of Dropout Methods for Deep Neural Networks
abstract: A comprehensive survey of dropout methods including standard dropout, variational dropout, concrete dropout, spatial dropout, and other variants for deep neural networks.
key_findings: Comprehensive taxonomy of dropout variants. Standard dropout less effective in convolutional layers due to spatial correlation. Spatial and structured dropout variants better suited for CNNs.
relationship_to_idea: Provides context on why dropout rate matters differently in convolutional vs fully-connected layers.

title: Efficient and Effective Dropout for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Proposes efficient dropout methods specifically designed for deep convolutional neural networks, addressing the inefficiency of standard dropout in CNNs.
key_findings: Standard dropout is inefficient in CNNs. Proposes targeted dropout strategies that are both computationally efficient and effective for regularization in deep CNNs.
relationship_to_idea: Directly relevant — addresses how dropout rate and strategy interact in CNN architectures.

title: Investigating the Relationship Between Dropout Regularization and Model Complexity in Neural Networks
abstract: Investigates the complex correlation between dropout rate and model complexity hyperparameters, questioning the assumption that increasing depth with higher dropout always helps.
key_findings: There exists an optimal dropout rate that maximizes test accuracy. Setting it incorrectly causes over-regularization. The relationship between dropout rate and model complexity is non-trivial and can be predicted with ML models.
relationship_to_idea: Directly supports the hypothesis — confirms that dropout rate selection significantly impacts performance and that 0.3 vs 0.5 can lead to meaningfully different outcomes.

title: Dropout Reduces Underfitting
abstract: Shows that dropout can reduce underfitting in addition to overfitting. Early dropout helps underfitting models fit better, late dropout improves generalization.
key_findings: Dropout scheduling matters: early dropout reduces underfitting, late dropout reduces overfitting. Challenges the view that dropout only helps with overfitting.
relationship_to_idea: Relevant context — dropout rate interacts with training schedule, suggesting that comparing fixed rates may miss temporal effects.

title: R-Drop: Regularized Dropout for Neural Networks
abstract: Proposes R-Drop which regularizes the output distributions of sub-models generated by dropout, forcing different dropout masks to produce consistent predictions.
key_findings: Adding KL-divergence loss between dropout sub-models improves regularization. Works across NLP, CV, and speech tasks.
relationship_to_idea: Alternative approach to improving dropout effectiveness — could serve as a comparison point beyond simple rate changes.

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: AlexNet — first large-scale CNN to win ImageNet. Used dropout in fully-connected layers with rate 0.5 to combat overfitting.
key_findings: Pioneered use of dropout (p=0.5) in CNN fully-connected layers. Dropout roughly doubled the number of iterations needed to converge but significantly reduced overfitting.
relationship_to_idea: Historical context — established p=0.5 as the default dropout rate for CNNs, which our experiment aims to compare against p=0.3.

title: DropBlock: A Regularization Method for Convolutional Networks
abstract: Proposes DropBlock which drops contiguous regions of feature maps rather than individual units, specifically designed for convolutional layers.
key_findings: Standard dropout ineffective in conv layers because spatially correlated features pass information through neighbors. DropBlock drops contiguous regions, significantly improving CNN regularization.
relationship_to_idea: Important context — suggests that standard dropout rate comparison in conv layers may be less impactful than in FC layers due to spatial correlation.

title: Efficient Object Localization Using Convolutional Networks
abstract: Introduces SpatialDropout which drops entire feature maps instead of individual pixels in CNNs, addressing the spatial correlation problem.
key_findings: Standard dropout in conv layers is ineffective because neighboring pixels share information. SpatialDropout drops entire feature maps, providing better regularization for CNNs.
relationship_to_idea: Relevant variant — when comparing dropout rates in CNNs, the type of dropout matters as much as the rate.

title: A Review on Dropout Regularization Approaches for Deep Neural Networks within the Scholarly Domain
abstract: Comprehensive review of dropout regularization approaches covering standard dropout, variants, and their effects on different neural network architectures.
key_findings: Dropout rates between 0.2-0.5 are typical. For conv layers, 0.2-0.3 recommended; for FC layers, 0.5 recommended. Optimal rate depends on architecture, dataset size, and layer type.
relationship_to_idea: Directly relevant — provides empirical guidelines that 0.3 is better for conv layers while 0.5 is better for FC layers, which is exactly what our experiment tests.

title: A Survey on Dropout Methods and Experimental Verification
abstract: Survey covering dropout methods with experimental verification across different architectures and tasks.
key_findings: Systematic experimental comparison of dropout methods. Confirms architecture-dependent optimal dropout rates and provides practical guidelines for dropout selection.
relationship_to_idea: Provides experimental methodology reference and confirms that systematic dropout rate comparison is a valid research direction.

title: Shakeout: A New Approach to Regularized Deep Neural Network Training
abstract: Proposes Shakeout which combines dropout with L1 and L2 regularization effects by randomly choosing to enhance or reverse the contribution of each unit.
key_findings: Combines dropout-like stochastic training with explicit regularization. Achieves L1+L2 regularization effect during training.
relationship_to_idea: Alternative regularization approach — provides context on dropout alternatives but less directly relevant to rate comparison.

title: Improved Regularization of Convolutional Neural Networks with Cutout
abstract: Proposes Cutout, a data augmentation technique that randomly masks square regions of input images during training, serving as a regularizer for CNNs.
key_findings: Input-level regularization by masking image patches. Complementary to dropout and achieves strong results on CIFAR-10/100.
relationship_to_idea: Data augmentation alternative to dropout — could serve as baseline comparison alongside dropout rate experiments.
